assistant_message_sections.title: There is still time to get ahead of this at home
assistant_message_sections.content: The priority is to control nausea, restore fluids, and monitor glucose before this becomes a bigger dehydration or hypoglycemia event.

assistant_message_sections.title: This is more than a poor appetite day
assistant_message_sections.content: In an ADC setting, nausea plus poor intake creates two risks at once for a diabetic patient: dehydration and unstable glucose.

assistant_message_sections.title: Order of operations
assistant_message_sections.content: Use the antiemetic early, switch to small frequent intake, and track orthostatic BP, urine output, and fingerstick glucose together.

assistant_message_sections.title: The goal is stability, not forcing big meals
assistant_message_sections.content: Even a few bites and a few sips at a time count if they help fluids and calories slowly come back up.

medication.issues: Continuing metformin while intake is poor can push both dehydration and low-glucose risk higher.
medication.adjustments: Before intake recovers, the trial team should clarify whether metformin should be held or retimed.

structured_output.nutrition_advice: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine a targeted antibody with a potent cytotoxic payload. While they can attack tumors effectively, off-target effects or payload release may also trigger gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, marrow, or lung toxicity. The core nutrition principles are: higher protein, easy digestion, small frequent meals, and side-effect-specific adjustments. Because ADC targets may be broadly expressed in the gastrointestinal tract, or because the gut lining turns over quickly, nausea, diarrhea, and reduced intake are common. Use small, frequent, bland meals; avoid greasy, fried, and spicy foods; and aim for 5 to 6 eating moments per day without overfilling. Prioritize steamed fish, poached chicken breast, tofu, steamed egg, and vitamin-rich gourd vegetables for higher-protein, easier-to-digest choices. If diarrhea becomes significant, watch for dehydration and electrolyte loss and use oral rehydration solution, or lightly salted rice broth. Avoid milk and dairy because lactose can worsen gut burden. If nausea is severe, avoid large amounts of fluid during meals and move soups and other liquid foods to at least 30 minutes before or after eating. Because ADC targets are widely expressed in the gastrointestinal tract, or because the gut lining turns over quickly, nausea, diarrhea, and reduced intake can show up early. The immediate priorities are smaller meals, steady hydration, and close tracking of both glucose swings and dehydration risk. Small frequent bland meals matter most: avoid greasy, fried, and spicy foods; prefer steamed fish, poached chicken breast, tofu, steamed egg, and vitamin-rich gourd vegetables.

health_guidance.summary: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine a targeted antibody with a potent cytotoxic payload. While they can attack tumors effectively, off-target effects or payload release may also trigger gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, marrow, or lung toxicity. The core nutrition principles are: higher protein, easy digestion, small frequent meals, and side-effect-specific adjustments. Emily's problem is not just 'poor appetite' — ADC GI toxicity, dehydration, and diabetes-related glucose swings are amplifying one another and need to be managed together.
